name: EchoNext Continuous D1 SetOperator (Primary Standard)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Continuous 8-D operator embeddings on clinical basis [I, II, V1-V6] provide rotation/permutation-invariant representations that outperform categorical baselines.
components_changed: Baseline standard: 8->64->64 MLP operator encoder, PhaseCNN response encoder, 2-layer Transformer d_model=192, attention pooling, Linear(256, 1) AF head.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Exact 1,027,009 trainable parameters; optimal permutation invariance and lead dropout robustness.

name: Matched Categorical Operator Control
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Discrete channel IDs fail to generalize to novel orientations or lead swaps compared to continuous coordinates.
components_changed: Operator encoder replaced with nn.Embedding(2, 64) and unknown operator sentinel buffer.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operator_ids: (B, M) int, mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Strong in-distribution performance on standard Lead I/II, but severe degradation on non-canonical orientations.

name: Operator-Ablated Control (Zero Coordinates)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Stripping operator identity degrades sensitivity to localized morphology variations (atrial flutter vs AF fibrillatory waves).
components_changed: Operator encoder ablated; replaced with constant zero tensor (64-D), testing purely unordered set pooling without coordinate identity.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Loss of lead-specific morphological distinction; serves as strict lower bound for set aggregation benefits.

name: 2D Continuous Operator (Frontal Plane Coordinates)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Restricting continuous operator representation to 2D frontal plane projection [cos θ, sin θ] retains limb lead geometric relationships with lower coordinate overhead.
components_changed: Operator encoder takes 2D vectors: Linear(2, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 2), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Equivalent limb lead interpolation to 8-D basis, but cannot represent precordial out-of-plane projections.

name: 3D Vectorcardiographic Continuous Operator (Frank XYZ)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Frank 3D orthogonal coordinate basis [X, Y, Z] models the physiological cardiac dipole more compactly than redundant 8-lead projections.
components_changed: Operator encoder takes 3D dipole direction vectors: Linear(3, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 3), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Improved physiological dipole orientation modeling, high robustness to electrode displacement.

name: 12-Lead Standard Clinical Basis (Redundant Limb & Precordial)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Full 12-lead basis (including redundant augmented limb leads III, aVR, aVL, aVF) improves transfer learning from 12-lead pretraining.
components_changed: Operator encoder takes 12-D vectors: Linear(12, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 12), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Slight parameter increase (+256); linear dependencies among limb leads handled via transformer self-attention.

name: Projective RP^7 Operator (Outer Product Matrix q q^T)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Projective space RP^7 formulation using rank-1 matrix q q^T provides strict mathematical polarity invariance (q -> -q leaves output identical).
components_changed: Operator encoder takes flattened 64-D outer product: Linear(64, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Strict sign invariance for inverted Holter electrode leads (e.g. Lead I reversed).

name: Unit-Sphere Normalized Continuous Operator (S^7)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Explicit unit-norm projection (q / ||q||_2) prevents gradient scaling artifacts caused by differing lead projection magnitudes.
components_changed: L2 normalization layer applied to operator coordinates prior to MLP projection.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: More stable optimization trajectories across diverse voltage amplitudes.

name: Continuous Operator with Stochastic Rotational Augmentation
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Injecting random 3D rotations SO(3) into operator coordinates during training prevents overfitting to rigid canonical electrode placements.
components_changed: Data augmentation: operators multiplied by random rotation matrix in SO(8) during training with angle sigma=5 degrees.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Improved robustness on external Holter cohorts (SHDB-AF) where electrode placement deviates from Einthoven.

name: Grassmannian Subspace Operator Gr(k, 8)
group: Group A: Core Operator Geometry & Continuous Basis Formulation
hypothesis: Representing simultaneous multi-lead acquisitions as a k-dimensional subspace on the Grassmann manifold Gr(k, 8) captures multi-channel correlation subspaces.
components_changed: Operator encoder maps projection matrix P = Q(Q^T Q)^-1 Q^T into subspace embedding vector.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), subspace_matrix: (B, 8, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Enhanced multi-lead fusion for 3+ lead acquisitions.

name: Linear Operator Projection (No Hidden Layer)
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: A single linear projection Linear(8, 64) is sufficient for operator coordinates, eliminating non-linear MLP distortion.
components_changed: Operator encoder simplified from 8->64->64 MLP to single Linear(8, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Faster forward pass (-4,176 parameters), but slightly lower expressive capacity for non-linear lead combinations.

name: Deep 3-Layer Operator MLP (8->64->128->64)
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: Deepening the operator encoder provides higher-order coordinate transformations that capture complex cardiac vector loops.
components_changed: Operator encoder expanded to Linear(8, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 128) -> GELU -> Linear(128, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Higher representational capacity; potential risk of overfitting on standard 2-channel Holter datasets.

name: Sinusoidal / Fourier Positional Operator Encoding
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: High-frequency Fourier feature mappings of operator angles resolve subtle angular differences between adjacent precordial leads.
components_changed: Continuous operator coordinates transformed via 16 Fourier frequencies before Linear(32, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Sharper angular distinction between closely spaced leads.

name: Operator Encoder with LayerNorm Normalization
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: LayerNorm inside the operator MLP stabilizes token embedding variance across variable batch sizes.
components_changed: Operator encoder: Linear(8, 64) -> LayerNorm(64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64) -> LayerNorm(64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Smoother gradient norms during BF16 mixed-precision training.

name: Operator Encoder with Dropout (p=0.1)
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: Dropout in the operator MLP prevents co-adaptation between specific coordinate axes and response features.
components_changed: Operator encoder incorporates nn.Dropout(0.1) after first GELU activation.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Improved generalization on small patient subsets.

name: Wide Operator MLP (8->128->128->64)
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: Wider intermediate hidden dimensions expand the geometric capacity of the coordinate embedding space.
components_changed: Operator encoder: Linear(8, 128) -> GELU -> Linear(128, 128) -> GELU -> Linear(128, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Modest parameter increase (+20,096 params); marginal gain on 2-lead Holters.

name: Operator Encoder with Learnable Lead Anchor Biases
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: Adding learnable bias offsets to the 8 standard clinical lead coordinates allows soft adaptation to empirical Holter distortions.
components_changed: Learnable Parameter(8, 8) additive bias table added to continuous operator coordinates.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Automated calibration of lead angle inaccuracies.

name: Residual MLP Operator Encoder
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: A residual skip connection inside the operator MLP preserves linear coordinate fidelity while adding non-linear correction terms.
components_changed: Operator encoder: Linear(8, 64) -> residual block (Linear(64, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64) + skip).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Preserves direct directional correspondence while providing non-linear warping.

name: Demographic-Conditioned Operator Encoder (Age/Sex Modulation)
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: Modulating operator coordinates by patient age and sex accounts for anatomical heart axis shifts (e.g. left axis deviation in elderly).
components_changed: Operator encoder concatenated with 2-D demographic vector [age, sex] -> Linear(10, 64) -> GELU -> Linear(64, 64).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), demographics: (B, 2), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Improved baseline specificity in elderly patients with structural heart axis shifts.

name: Identity Zero-Param Operator Embedding (Direct Coordinate Zero-Pad)
group: Group B: Operator Encoder Architectures & Capacity
hypothesis: Directly zero-padding the 8-D operator coordinates to 64-D without trainable weights tests if learned transformation is necessary.
components_changed: Operator encoder replaced with deterministic padding: [q, zeros(56)]. Trainable parameters = 0 in operator encoder.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Requires Transformer encoder to learn coordinate projection directly; slower convergence.

name: 64 Nyström Landmark Phase-KME Approximation
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Halving Nyström landmarks from 128 to 64 speeds up phase extraction with minimal loss in kernel approximation fidelity.
components_changed: Phase response dimension reduced from 128 to 64. PhaseCNN input adjusted to Conv1d(64, 128, 1).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 64), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: 50% reduction in phase cache storage; slight drop in fine P-wave morphology resolution.

name: 256 Nyström Landmark Phase-KME Approximation
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Doubling Nyström landmarks to 256 captures subtle high-frequency atrial fibrillation fibrillatory f-waves.
components_changed: Phase response dimension increased from 128 to 256. PhaseCNN input Conv1d(256, 128, 1).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 256), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Higher kernel fidelity (relative error < 0.0001), increased preprocessing time.

name: 8 Phase Cells Cardiac Cycle Quantization
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Coarser phase partitioning (8 cells instead of 16) provides sufficient resolution for ventricular rhythm while reducing temporal dimensionality.
components_changed: Response tensor shape changed to (B, M, 8, 128).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 8, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: 40% faster PhaseCNN forward pass, but loss of distinct atrial P-wave phase cells.

name: 32 Phase Cells Cardiac Cycle Quantization
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Finer phase partitioning (32 cells) enables sub-millisecond tracking of atrial repolarization dynamics.
components_changed: Response tensor shape changed to (B, M, 32, 128).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 32, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Higher temporal resolution; larger memory footprint.

name: Inverse Multiquadric (IMQ) Kernel with c^2=0.5
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Narrower length-scale (c^2=0.5 vs default 1.0) sharpens sensitivity to local QRS peak variations.
components_changed: Phase kernel parameter: c^2 length-scale decreased to 0.5 in IMQ formula k(x, y) = (1 + ||x-y||^2 / c^2)^-1/2.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Sharper landmark differentiation; potential sensitivity to baseline EMG noise.

name: Inverse Multiquadric (IMQ) Kernel with c^2=2.0
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Broader length-scale (c^2=2.0) smooths out high-frequency muscular noise in wearable Holter leads.
components_changed: Phase kernel parameter: c^2 length-scale increased to 2.0.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Enhanced noise robustness; slightly reduced discrimination between normal sinus P-waves and f-waves.

name: Gaussian Radial Basis Function (RBF) Kernel Mean Embedding
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Gaussian RBF kernel k(x, y) = exp(-gamma ||x-y||^2) yields tighter feature localization than heavy-tailed IMQ.
components_changed: Nyström kernel formulation switched from IMQ to Gaussian RBF with gamma = 1 / (2 * sigma^2).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Faster decay for distant waveforms; verified against IMQ baseline.

name: Direct PCHIP Normalized Waveform Samples (No Kernel Embedding)
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Evaluating raw 128-sample PCHIP beat waveforms directly tests whether non-linear Hilbert space kernel mapping is necessary.
components_changed: Responses are 16 phase cells x 128 raw PCHIP interpolated voltage samples (no Nyström projection).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Lower specificity on noisy segments; demonstrates the noise-filtering benefit of Phase-KME.

name: Vector Quantization (VQ) Dictionary Codebook Embedding
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Discrete VQ codebook centroids provide interpretable morphological prototype representations.
components_changed: Nyström landmark map replaced with 128-entry VQ codebook with soft assignment weights.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Highly interpretable codebook prototypes; slightly lower gradient smoothness.

name: Unwhitened Phase Atom Sampling
group: Group C: Phase Representation, KME Landmarks, and Atom Sampling
hypothesis: Ablating ZCA/PCA whitening on phase atoms exposes how correlated physiological features impact kernel conditioning.
components_changed: Phase-KME landmark fitting uses raw unwhitened phase atoms (covariance inverse root omitted).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Ill-conditioned kernel Gram matrix, slower optimizer convergence.

name: Single-Block Circular PhaseCNN (Reduced Depth)
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: A single circular residual block provides adequate receptive field across the 16 phase cells while halving response encoder parameters.
components_changed: PhaseCNN blocks reduced from 2 to 1 CircularResidualBlock(128).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Faster execution (-98,560 params); slightly lower feature richness.

name: Dual-Moment (Mean + Variance) Phase Response Pooling
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Extracting both mean and variance across the 16 phase cells captures morphological variability and disorganized fibrillatory waves characteristic of AF.
components_changed: Response encoder pools both mean and std across phase cells, projected via Linear(256, 128).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Substantial gain in detecting paroxysmal AF where beat-to-beat morphology fluctuates irregularly.

name: Deep 3-Block Circular PhaseCNN
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Deepening PhaseCNN to 3 circular blocks captures multi-scale phase interactions spanning the full P-QRS-T trajectory.
components_changed: PhaseCNN blocks increased to 3 CircularResidualBlock(128).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Marginal gains on complex arrhythmia patterns; higher computational load.

name: Standard Zero-Padding Residual Blocks (No Circular Wrap-Around)
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Circular padding is physically essential to respect the continuous closed loop of the cardiac cycle; zero padding causes boundary artifacts at phase 0/16.
components_changed: CircularResidualBlock replaced with StandardResidualBlock using zero padding (F.pad zero).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Discontinuity artifacts between end of T-wave and start of P-wave, degrading P-wave detection.

name: Dilated 1D ConvNet Response Encoder
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Exponentially dilated convolutions (dilation=1, 2, 4) rapidly span the entire 16-cell cardiac cycle with fewer parameters.
components_changed: PhaseCNN residual blocks incorporate progressive dilation rates 1, 2.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Broader receptive field; maintains high performance on irregular brady/tachycardia.

name: Bidirectional GRU Phase Sequence Encoder
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Recurrent modeling of the 16 phase cells via BiGRU captures sequential temporal transitions across the cardiac cycle.
components_changed: PhaseCNN replaced with nn.GRU(128, 64, bidirectional=True, batch_first=True) over 16 phase tokens.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Good sequential modeling; slower GPU execution due to recurrent bottleneck.

name: Order-Preserving Beat Sequence Encoder
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Preserving the sequential temporal order of phase transitions using causal 1D depthwise convolutions captures rhythm irregularity directly within the response representation.
components_changed: Sequential causal 1D depthwise convolution blocks applied across the ordered phase trajectory before response pooling.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Enhanced sensitivity to non-stationary irregular rhythm onset within 30s windows.

name: Phase-Cell Self-Attention Encoder (1-Layer Transformer)
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Self-attention directly across the 16 phase cells learns dynamic correlations between atrial P-wave and ventricular T-wave phases.
components_changed: PhaseCNN replaced with 1-layer TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model=128, nhead=4).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Flexible all-to-all phase correlation modeling; slightly higher attention compute.

name: PhaseCNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) Channel Attention
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: SE blocks recalibrate channel-wise feature responses, emphasizing discriminative Nyström landmark dimensions.
components_changed: SE attention blocks (reduction ratio 4) added after each circular residual block in PhaseCNN.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Adaptive feature gating; modest parameter increment (+8,192).

name: Operator-Cross-Gated Response Encoder (Early FiLM Modulation)
group: Group D: Response Encoder Architectures & Phase Dynamics
hypothesis: Modulating PhaseCNN intermediate features by the operator continuous vector via FiLM (Feature-wise Linear Modulation) tailors morphology extraction to lead orientation early.
components_changed: FiLM affine modulation: gamma(q) * x + beta(q) applied inside PhaseCNN residual blocks.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Strong orientation-conditioned feature extraction; high multi-lead synergy.

name: Unweighted Masked Mean Pooling (DeepSets Baseline)
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Learned query attention pooling is unnecessary; simple unweighted masked mean pooling provides sufficient permutation-invariant aggregation.
components_changed: MultiheadAttention pooling replaced with masked mean pooling over active measurement tokens. pool_query and pool ablated.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Equal weighting of all leads regardless of signal quality or noise level; lower specificity on noisy leads.

name: DeepSets Max Pooling
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Max pooling across channels emphasizes the lead with the clearest AF diagnostic signature (e.g. clearest f-waves in Lead V1).
components_changed: MultiheadAttention pooling replaced with element-wise masked max pooling.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: High sensitivity to localized rhythm abnormalities; susceptible to isolated lead artifact spikes.

name: Cardinality-Normalized Sum Pooling
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Sum pooling normalized by sqrt(|S|) balances signal accumulation with cardinality invariance across 1-lead and 2-lead acquisitions.
components_changed: Set pooling: sum(active_tokens) / sqrt(active_count).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Smooth scaling when transitioning between single-channel and multi-channel monitoring.

name: Multi-Query Attention Pooling (4 Learned Queries)
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Multiple learned pooling queries attend to distinct diagnostic facets (e.g. Query 1: atrial rhythm, Query 2: QRS morphology, Query 3: noise SQI).
components_changed: pool_query expanded to (1, 4, 192). Pooled output flattened to 4*192=768 -> Linear(768, 256) -> GELU.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Richer multi-perspective latent representation (+148,416 params).

name: Generalized Mean (GeM) Learnable Power Pooling
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Learnable p-norm pooling (GeM) smoothly interpolates between average pooling (p=1) and max pooling (p->inf).
components_changed: Pooling operation: (1/|S| sum x^p)^(1/p) with learnable parameter p initialized to 3.0.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Adaptive interpolation between dominant lead detection and global consensus.

name: Cross-Lead Bilinear Outer Product Pooling
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Second-order bilinear pooling captures cross-channel covariance matrices that reflect spatial cardiac axis orientation.
components_changed: Channel tokens pooled via normalized outer-product covariance matrix projected to 256-D.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Direct extraction of spatial inter-lead correlation features.

name: Phase-Wise Attention Pooling (Joint Channel-Phase Attention)
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Attending jointly across all channels and phase cells simultaneously captures phase-specific lead discrepancies without pre-collapsing phase dimensions.
components_changed: Phase cells not collapsed before transformer; tokens are (B, M*16, 192), cross-attention pooling operates over all M*16 tokens jointly.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Fine-grained phase-lead interaction modeling; higher FLOP budget (57.4 MFLOPs).

name: Set Transformer with Induced Set Attention Blocks (ISAB)
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Induced Set Attention Blocks (ISAB with 8 inducing points) reduce attention complexity to O(M * I) while preserving expressiveness.
components_changed: Set transformer replaced with ISAB blocks using 8 learned inducing point vectors.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Sub-quadratic scaling; primarily advantageous for large sets (M > 8).

name: Cardinality-Conditioned Set Attention Pooling
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Conditioning the learned pooling query on the active lead count (|S| = 1 vs 2) prevents single-lead under-confidence.
components_changed: pool_query modulated by an embedding of the integer active channel count.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Eliminates confidence drop when evaluating on isolated single channels.

name: Gated Attention Pooling (Ilse et al. Multiple-Instance Learning)
group: Group E: Set Aggregation, Pooling, and Permutation Invariance
hypothesis: Gated tanh-sigmoid attention weights (a = softmax(w^T (tanh(V h) * sigm(U h)))) suppress noisy/uninformative channels dynamically.
components_changed: MultiheadAttention replaced with trainable MIL gated attention network.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Explicit, inspectable scalar attention weight per lead for clinical interpretability.

name: 1-Layer Transformer Set Encoder (Reduced Depth)
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: For small set cardinalities (M=2), a single self-attention layer suffices for cross-lead interaction.
components_changed: num_layers reduced from 2 to 1 in TransformerEncoder.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: 36% parameter reduction (-369,408 params) with minor reduction in cross-lead reasoning.

name: 4-Layer Deep Transformer Set Encoder
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Deepening the set transformer to 4 layers enables hierarchical compositional reasoning across leads.
components_changed: num_layers increased from 2 to 4 in TransformerEncoder.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Higher capacity (+738,816 params); requires careful dropout to avoid overfitting.

name: No Transformer Set Encoder (Direct Masked Mean Pooling Control)
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Evaluating direct projection and masked mean pooling without any Transformer layers determines the exact performance gain attributable to self-attention.
components_changed: TransformerEncoder and MultiheadAttention pooling completely ablated; Linear(192, 256) projection + masked mean pooling directly to head.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Ultra-lightweight baseline (284k params); isolates the specific value-add of Transformer self-attention.

name: Narrow Transformer Latent (d_model = 128, nhead = 4)
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Compacting the token dimension to 128 reduces computational footprint while matching performance.
components_changed: d_model=128, dim_feedforward=256 in TransformerEncoderLayer. Operator embedding 32-D, PhaseCNN head 96-D.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: 33% parameter savings; slight drop on ambiguous multi-lead patterns.

name: Wide Transformer Latent (d_model = 256, nhead = 8)
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Expanding token dimension to 256 with 8 attention heads accommodates richer multi-lead interaction subspaces.
components_changed: d_model=256, nhead=8, dim_feedforward=512 in TransformerEncoderLayer.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Increased representational bandwidth; higher peak GPU memory.

name: Pre-LayerNorm Transformer Architecture
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Pre-LN (norm_first=True) prevents vanishing/exploding gradients in BF16 mixed-precision training compared to standard Post-LN.
components_changed: TransformerEncoderLayer configured with norm_first=True.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Enhanced gradient stability, zero divergence in early warmup epochs.

name: Residual Token Pathway SetOperator
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Adding an explicit residual skip pathway around the Transformer set encoder (encoded = encoder(tokens) + tokens) prevents attention oversmoothing and preserves local lead fidelity.
components_changed: Residual skip connection added: encoded = set_encoder(tokens) + tokens before attention pooling.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Prevents representation collapse on uniform inputs; preserves identical 1,027,009 parameter count.

name: Linearized Kernel Attention (Performer / Cosine Sim)
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Linearized kernel attention eliminates quadratic softmax memory scaling.
components_changed: Softmax attention in TransformerEncoder replaced with positive random feature (PRF) linear attention.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Exact O(N) memory scaling; negligible difference at N=2, scalable to 12-lead setups.

name: Relative Geometric Angular Bias in Self-Attention
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Injecting the continuous angular difference cos(theta_i - theta_j) directly into the self-attention logits biases attention towards orthogonal lead pairs.
components_changed: Attention logit matrix modified: A_ij = (Q_i K_j^T / sqrt(d)) + lambda * (q_i . q_j).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Prioritizes complementary perpendicular lead perspectives (e.g. Lead I and aVF).

name: Stochastic Depth (DropPath = 0.1) in Set Encoder
group: Group F: Set Transformer Depth, Dimension, and Attention Mechanics
hypothesis: Randomly dropping entire transformer encoder layers during training acts as an effective regularizer against co-dependency.
components_changed: DropPath probability p=0.1 applied to TransformerEncoder residual branches.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Improved test set generalization on small cohort splits.

name: Explicit RR Statistical Branch Multimodal Fusion
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Concatenating 36-D standardized RR interval statistics (mean, SD, RMSSD, Shannon entropy, etc.) at the latent head combines ventricular rhythm irregularity with P-wave morphology.
components_changed: Head expanded from Linear(256, 1) to Linear(256 + 36, 1) to accept RR statistical feature vector.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_features: (B, 36), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Significant boost in AF sensitivity during episodes with subtle f-waves but pronounced RR irregularity.

name: Cross-Attention Fusion (RR Token to Morphology Set Tokens)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Allowing an RR interval token to cross-attend into morphology tokens dynamically modulates P-wave search based on rhythm regularity.
components_changed: RR features projected to 192-D token; cross-attention layer between RR token and measurement tokens.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_features: (B, 36), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Morphology encoder focuses on P-wave presence only when RR regularity is borderline.

name: Early Fusion (RR Context Appended to Operator Coordinates)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Injecting patient RR summary statistics into the operator MLP provides rhythm context at the earliest token creation level.
components_changed: Operator encoder input expanded from 8 to 8 + 36 = 44 dimensions.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_features: (B, 36), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Joint rhythm-morphology token space from the first layer.

name: Gated Adaptive Modality Fusion (Learned Scalar Gating)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: A learned sigmoid gating scalar g = sigmoid(W [h_morph, h_rr]) suppresses the morphology branch when waveform noise SQI is severe.
components_changed: Adaptive gating module: out = g * head_morph(latent) + (1-g) * head_rr(rr_features).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_features: (B, 36), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Automated fallback to RR baseline under intense motion artifact.

name: Late Ensemble Averaging (Independent SetOperator + HGB RR)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Late probability averaging of an independently trained SetOperator and Histogram Gradient Boosting (HGB) model avoids co-adaptation.
components_changed: Post-hoc ensemble: P_final = 0.5 * P_SetOperator + 0.5 * P_HGB_RR.
inputs: SetOperator logits + precomputed HGB probability scores
expected_behavior: Solid baseline calibration; zero training co-dependency.

name: Non-Linear MLP Multimodal Fusion Head (256+36 -> 128 -> 1)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: A 2-layer MLP head models non-linear interactions between RR irregularity metrics and morphology features.
components_changed: Fusion head: Linear(292, 128) -> GELU -> Linear(128, 1).
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_features: (B, 36), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Captures joint non-linear decision boundaries for complex paroxysmal episodes.

name: Modality Dropout Regularization (p=0.2)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Randomly dropping either the morphology branch or RR branch during training forces both pathways to maintain high stand-alone competence.
components_changed: During training, morphology latent zeroed with p=0.2, or RR branch zeroed with p=0.2, with modality presence flags.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_features: (B, 36), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Prevents over-reliance on RR intervals during frequent ventricular ectopy.

name: Sequential RR Interval Transformer Branch (Raw 60-Beat Sequence)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: A 1D Transformer over the raw sequence of 60 beat-to-beat RR intervals captures higher-order rhythm grammar than 36 static summary moments.
components_changed: Static 36-D RR replaced with 1-layer TransformerEncoder over 60 RR interval scalars.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_sequence: (B, 60, 1), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Superior discrimination of respiratory sinus arrhythmia vs true atrial fibrillation.

name: Poincaré Plot 2D CNN Fusion Branch
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Encoding the 2D Poincaré scatter plot (RR_n vs RR_n+1) via a small 2D CNN captures non-linear phase space cluster dispersion directly.
components_changed: Poincaré 32x32 density histogram processed via 2-layer CNN into 64-D vector fused with morphology latent.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), poincare_img: (B, 1, 32, 32), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Fast, visual capture of fan-shaped AF scatter patterns.

name: Rhythm-Prior Logit Fusion (Additive Log-Odds Prior)
group: Group G: Multimodal RR & Morphology Fusion Architectures
hypothesis: Injecting the log-odds prediction from the frozen RR baseline as an additive prior logit (logit_final = logit_morph + w * logit_rr) preserves Bayesian optimality.
components_changed: Fixed additive fusion: logit = model.head(latent) + alpha * logit_rr with learnable scalar alpha.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), rr_logit: (B, 1), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Strict Bayesian calibration with minimal parameter change (+1 scalar).

name: Per-Channel Raw 1D ResNet Encoder SetOperator
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: An 8-block 1D ResNet extracting 128-D response tokens directly from raw 1D voltage waveforms (6000 samples @ 200 Hz) eliminates dependence on Phase-KME preprocessing.
components_changed: PhaseCNN replaced with per-channel 8-block 1D ResNet stem and convolutional blocks. Set Transformer and head unchanged.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Direct end-to-end waveform learning; higher FLOP count (2.92 GFLOPs) and sensitive to high-frequency EMG noise.

name: Shared Raw ResNet with Continuous FiLM Modulation
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: FiLM modulation of intermediate ResNet feature maps by operator coordinates allows a single shared convolutional backbone to adapt dynamically to lead orientation.
components_changed: 1D ResNet incorporates FiLM layers after each residual stage, conditioned on operator coordinates.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Orientation-aware convolutional feature filtering.

name: Multi-Scale 1D ConvNet Raw Waveform Front-End
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Parallel multi-scale 1D convolution filters (0.05s, 0.2s, 1.0s kernel windows) extract QRS, P-wave, and baseline wander features simultaneously.
components_changed: Initial ResNet stem replaced with multi-scale inception-style parallel 1D convolution bank.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Excellent separation of sharp QRS spikes from low-amplitude undulating f-waves.

name: SincNet Parameterized Bandpass Filter Front-End
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Learnable SincNet bandpass filter banks constrain initial convolutional filters to physiologically meaningful frequency bands (0.5-40 Hz).
components_changed: First 1D conv layer replaced with learnable SincNet parameterized sinc functions.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Strict frequency containment; robust against powerline hum and high-frequency noise.

name: Wavelet Scattering Transform Front-End
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Predefined 1D Wavelet Scattering coefficients provide translation-invariant, stable multi-scale representations without learned conv weights.
components_changed: Raw waveform mapped to order-2 wavelet scattering coefficients before Linear(J*Q, 128) projection.
inputs: scattering_coeffs: (B, M, S_dim), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: High mathematical stability against time-warping and baseline wander.

name: Hybrid Dual-Stream (Raw Waveform + Phase-KME) Encoder
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Combining raw time-domain waveforms with phase-aligned Nyström kernel embeddings provides complementary local temporal and global morphological features.
components_changed: Dual response encoder: 64-D from 1D ResNet + 64-D from PhaseCNN concatenated into 128-D response token.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Best-of-both-worlds feature representation; higher memory requirements.

name: STFT Spectrogram 2D ConvNet Front-End
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Time-frequency STFT spectrograms directly visualize the characteristic 4-8 Hz fibrillatory power spectrum of atrial fibrillation.
components_changed: Waveforms transformed via STFT into 2D spectrogram images, processed via 2D ConvNet into 128-D tokens.
inputs: spectrograms: (B, M, F, T), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Direct spectral tracking of AF fibrillatory peak frequency.

name: PatchTST 1D Patch-Based Waveform Tokenizer
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Slicing raw 6000-sample ECG into non-overlapping 200-sample (1-second) patches encoded via linear projection bypasses CNN inductive biases.
components_changed: 1D Patch embedding: Linear(200, 128) across 30 patches per channel.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Pure transformer tokenization; fast execution.

name: Raw ResNet with Squeeze-and-Excitation Temporal Attention
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: SE temporal channel attention inside the 1D ResNet highlights critical arrhythmia transition windows.
components_changed: SE residual blocks incorporated throughout the 8-block 1D ResNet.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Sharper temporal focus on intermittent arrhythmia bursts.

name: Dilated Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) Waveform Encoder
group: Group H: Raw Waveform & Hybrid Feature Encoders
hypothesis: Causal dilated convolutions across the 30-second waveform achieve receptive fields exceeding 6000 samples with low parameter count.
components_changed: Raw encoder uses 6 dilated residual TCN blocks with dilation rates 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
inputs: raw_waveforms: (B, M, 6000), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: Large temporal receptive field; efficient memory scaling.

name: Linear(256, 1) AF Diagnostic Head (Canonical Standard)
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: A single linear projection directly from the 256-D latent prevents head overfitting and preserves linear separability.
components_changed: Baseline standard: Linear(256, 1) logit projection.
inputs: latent: (B, 256)
expected_behavior: Strict baseline standard (257 parameters in head).

name: ResNet + Residual MLP Classification Head
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: A 2-layer residual MLP classification head with skip connections (Linear(256, 256) -> GELU -> Linear(256, 256) + skip -> GELU -> Linear(256, 1)) separates subtle non-linear boundary cases.
components_changed: Head replaced with residual MLP block: 2 x Linear(256, 256) with skip connection.
inputs: latent: (B, 256)
expected_behavior: Higher non-linear boundary resolution (+131,584 params); tested in Stage 1.

name: Post-Hoc Temperature Scaling Calibration
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Post-hoc Platt temperature scaling (logit / T) optimized on validation NLL resolves overconfident predictions without altering model weights.
components_changed: Post-processing: single scalar temperature T fitted on validation set logits.
inputs: logits: (B,)
expected_behavior: Slashes Expected Calibration Error (ECE < 0.03); maintains ranking metrics (AUROC/AUPRC).

name: Isotonic Regression Non-Parametric Calibration
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Non-parametric isotonic regression recalibrates non-monotonic distortions in predicted probability distributions.
components_changed: Post-processing: isotonic regression mapping fitted on validation probabilities.
inputs: probabilities: (B,)
expected_behavior: Near-zero validation ECE; requires sufficient validation event counts.

name: Monte Carlo Dropout Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Retaining dropout at inference across 10 forward passes estimates epistemic uncertainty, identifying out-of-distribution artifact segments.
components_changed: Inference protocol: 10 stochastic forward passes with dropout p=0.1; reports mean probability and variance.
inputs: responses: (B, M, 16, 128), operators: (B, M, 8), mask: (B, M)
expected_behavior: High predictive variance on severely noisy Holter segments; flags indeterminate predictions.

name: Evidential Deep Learning Uncertainty Head (Beta Prior)
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Predicting Beta distribution concentration parameters (alpha, beta) via an evidential head provides analytical closed-form epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty.
components_changed: Head outputs 2 parameters [alpha, beta] via Softplus; loss combines Type II maximum likelihood and KL divergence.
inputs: latent: (B, 256)
expected_behavior: Single-pass uncertainty estimation without Monte Carlo sampling overhead.

name: Heteroscedastic Gaussian Logit Uncertainty Head
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Predicting logit mean mu and input-dependent variance sigma^2 captures window-specific observation noise.
components_changed: Head outputs [mu, log_var] via Linear(256, 2); loss uses Monte Carlo logit sampling during training.
inputs: latent: (B, 256)
expected_behavior: Learns to assign higher variance to high-noise segments automatically.

name: Chow's Selective Classification Abstention Head
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Providing an explicit abstention option (indeterminate / uninterpretable) when posterior probability falls in [0.5 - delta, 0.5 + delta] guarantees 100% specificity.
components_changed: Decision rule incorporates Chow's optimal reject rule under loss function L(reject) = c.
inputs: logits: (B,)
expected_behavior: Eliminates false alarms on ambiguous segments; preserves uninterpretable time in monitoring denominator.

name: Multi-Task Auxiliary Head (Simultaneous AF & Heart Rate Regression)
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Auxiliary prediction of instantaneous ventricular heart rate regularizes latent representations toward clinically relevant cardiac dynamics.
components_changed: Dual head: head_af: Linear(256, 1), head_hr: Linear(256, 1); joint loss = BCE + 0.1 * MSE(HR).
inputs: latent: (B, 256)
expected_behavior: Richer latent features; improved generalization on extreme tachy/bradycardia.

name: 5-Seed Deep Ensemble with Epistemic Disagreement Voting
group: Group I: Diagnostic Head, Latent Calibration, and Uncertainty
hypothesis: Ensembling 5 independently seeded A001 models (seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4) provides strong uncertainty boundaries and minimizes false positive spikes.
components_changed: Ensemble averaging over 5 trained checkpoints.
inputs: 5 x (responses, operators, mask)
expected_behavior: +1.5% AUROC gain, robust variance estimation across diverse patient anatomies.

name: Binary Cross Entropy with Logits (Canonical Baseline Loss)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Standard unweighted BCE provides unbiased maximum likelihood estimation under balanced patient-weighted sampling.
components_changed: Baseline standard: nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss() with patient assigned-duration weights.
inputs: logits: (B,), targets: (B,)
expected_behavior: Standard optimization baseline; requires patient weighting to avoid file-length bias.

name: Class-Balanced Weighted BCE Loss (Inverse Frequency)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Weighting AF positive windows by inverse prevalence compensates for low AF burden in paroxysmal cohorts.
components_changed: pos_weight parameter set to (N_negative / N_positive) in BCEWithLogitsLoss.
inputs: logits: (B,), targets: (B,)
expected_behavior: Increases sensitivity to isolated short AF bursts; increases false alarm rate on non-AF controls.

name: Focal Loss (gamma = 2.0, alpha = 0.25)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Focal loss down-weights easy sinus rhythm windows, focusing gradients on ambiguous transition boundaries.
components_changed: Loss function switched to Focal Loss: FL(p_t) = -alpha_t (1 - p_t)^gamma log(p_t) with gamma=2.0, alpha=0.25.
inputs: logits: (B,), targets: (B,)
expected_behavior: Sharper decision boundary around episode onset/offset transitions.

name: Asymmetric Loss (Higher False Negative Penalty)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Clinically penalizing false negatives (missed AF) 3x more heavily than false alarms prioritizes stroke prevention sensitivity.
components_changed: Asymmetric loss penalty: loss = - [3 * y log(p) + (1-y) log(1-p)].
inputs: logits: (B,), targets: (B,)
expected_behavior: Near-100% episode recall; lower specificity on non-AF negative controls.

name: Symmetric Bernoulli KL Permutation Regularization (J_sym)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Penalizing symmetric Bernoulli KL divergence between original and permuted channel ordering enforces exact permutation invariance.
components_changed: Regularization term: L_total = L_BCE + 0.5 * symmetric_bernoulli_kl(logit_orig, logit_perm).
inputs: responses, operators, permuted_responses, permuted_operators
expected_behavior: Guarantees zero logit discrepancy under measurement order permutations.

name: Auxiliary Continuous Operator Reconstruction Loss
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Predicting operator coordinates q from the pooled latent regularizes the Transformer set encoder to retain spatial orientation awareness.
components_changed: Auxiliary linear head: Linear(256, 8); loss = L_BCE + 0.1 * MSE(q_pred, q_true).
inputs: responses, operators, targets
expected_behavior: Enforces preservation of lead orientation information in pooled latent space.

name: Auxiliary Waveform Reconstruction Decoder Loss (Full 12-Lead)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Co-training with a 12-lead reconstruction decoder forces the latent representation to retain full morphological fidelity.
components_changed: Reconstruction decoder active during training: Linear(256, 12*625) + Conv1D refine; loss = L_BCE + 0.1 * L_reconstruction.
inputs: responses, operators, target_12lead_ecg
expected_behavior: Reconstruction decoder active in training only; diagnostic parameters remain 1,027,009.

name: Contrastive Representation Loss (InfoNCE Across Subsets)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: InfoNCE contrastive loss across different lead subsets of the same patient window aligns single-lead and two-lead representations.
components_changed: Contrastive loss: sim(latent_ch0, latent_ch1) maximized against in-batch negatives.
inputs: responses_ch0, responses_ch1
expected_behavior: Tight cluster alignment between single-channel and multi-channel latents.

name: Label Smoothing Regularization (epsilon = 0.05)
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: Label smoothing (y_smooth = y * 0.9 + 0.05) prevents logit overconfidence on ambiguous episode transition boundaries.
components_changed: Targets smoothed: 0 -> 0.05, 1 -> 0.95 in BCEWithLogitsLoss.
inputs: logits: (B,), targets: (B,)
expected_behavior: Reduced logit magnitude, improved validation calibration without post-processing.

name: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) Optimizer
group: Group J: Loss Functions, Supervisions, and Regularization
hypothesis: SAM optimizer seeks uniformly flat loss minima, improving generalizability across disparate external Holter datasets.
components_changed: Optimizer switched from AdamW to SAM(AdamW, rho=0.05).
inputs: Standard training batches
expected_behavior: 2x training forward/backward steps; higher out-of-distribution transfer to SHDB-AF.

name: 3-Epoch Cyclic Acquisition Schedule (Ch0 / Ch1 / Both)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Systematically cycling training windows across [Channel 0 only, Channel 1 only, Both channels] guarantees balanced representation across all acquisition topologies.
components_changed: Baseline training protocol: Epoch 1 (Ch0), Epoch 2 (Ch1), Epoch 3 (Both).
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Guarantees zero bias toward 2-lead setups; robust single-lead fallback.

name: Uniform Stochastic Channel Dropout (Bernoulli p=0.5)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Randomly masking active channels with independent probability p=0.5 during every training step improves robustness against dynamic channel dropouts.
components_changed: Channel mask generated via Bernoulli(0.5) per active channel, ensuring at least one channel remains active.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Higher single-channel accuracy without explicit 3-epoch cyclic scheduling.

name: Extreme Single-Lead Training Protocol (Always 1 Channel Active)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Restricting training exclusively to single-lead observations trains the model as a strict single-channel expert that generalizes to multi-channel test sets.
components_changed: During training, one channel is always randomly masked out (set size |S| = 1 strictly).
inputs: responses: (B, 1, 16, 128), operators: (B, 1, 8), mask: (B, 1)
expected_behavior: Optimal single-lead performance; slightly underutilizes cross-lead spatial correlations.

name: Asymmetric Channel Noise Injection (Gaussian Noise on Ch1)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Simulating asymmetric lead quality (clean Lead I, degraded Lead II with sigma=0.2 noise) trains attention pooling to down-weight noisy leads.
components_changed: Gaussian noise N(0, 0.2) injected into Channel 1 responses during training.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Attention pooling automatically shifts weight away from the corrupted channel.

name: Baseline Wander & Motion Artifact Injection
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Adding low-frequency sinusoidal wander (0.1-0.5 Hz) and random baseline steps replicates real-world Holter motion artifacts.
components_changed: Synthetic motion artifact augmentations added during raw waveform / phase feature generation.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Drastically reduces false alarms on physical activity and turning in bed.

name: Electrode Disconnection Simulation (Zero / Flatline Inactive Lead)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Simulating sudden lead disconnection (flatline 0 mV) verifies that the network does not hallucinate rhythm on disconnected channels.
components_changed: Simulated lead disconnect: response zeroed, available flag set to False.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Strict indeterminate handling when all leads disconnect; zero false positive AF.

name: Channel Swap Augmentation (Lead I <-> Lead II Inversion)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Swapping Lead I and Lead II indices along with corresponding operator coordinates verifies that prediction is invariant to channel indexing.
components_changed: Data augmentation: channel 0 and 1 tensors swapped with p=0.5 during training.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Exact numerical invariance under channel index permutation.

name: Dynamic Signal Quality Index (SQI) Attention Weighting
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Weighting channel token representations by an explicit SQI metric (0.0 to 1.0) biases set attention toward clean channels.
components_changed: Tokens multiplied by sqrt(SQI) prior to Transformer set encoder.
inputs: responses, operators, sqi_weights: (B, M), mask
expected_behavior: Suppresses contaminated channels during intense patient motion.

name: Scheduled Lead Dropout Decay (Curriculum p=0.8 -> 0.2)
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Curriculum learning starting with high channel dropout (p=0.8) builds strong single-lead foundations before introducing multi-lead synergy (p=0.2).
components_changed: Dropout probability annealed linearly from 0.8 at Epoch 1 to 0.2 at final epoch.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Smoother optimization and higher final joint-lead accuracy.

name: Adversarial FGSM Operator Coordinate Perturbation
group: Group K: Channel Robustness, Missing Leads, and Dropout Schedules
hypothesis: Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) perturbations on continuous operator coordinates during training builds worst-case geometric robustness.
components_changed: Adversarial training step: q_adv = q + epsilon * sign(grad_q(loss)) with epsilon=0.05.
inputs: responses, operators, mask
expected_behavior: Immunity to empirical electrode displacement up to 15 degrees.

name: D0 Raw Thresholding (Independent Per-Window Argmax)
group: Group L: Temporal Smoothing, Markov Decoding, and HSMM (D0, D1, D2)
hypothesis: Raw window-level argmax thresholding serves as the unregularized temporal baseline; sensitive to isolated false-positive spikes.
components_changed: Baseline standard: binary decision = (probability >= threshold). No temporal filtering.
inputs: Window probability predictions
expected_behavior: High episode fragmentation, elevated false positive episode counts, baseline reference.

name: D1 Binary Median Filter (Width = 3 Windows / 90 Seconds)
group: Group L: Temporal Smoothing, Markov Decoding, and HSMM (D0, D1, D2)
hypothesis: A 3-window median filter eliminates isolated 30-second false alarms while preserving true episodes >= 60 seconds.
components_changed: D1 post-processing: running binary median filter over odd window width W=3.
inputs: Window binary classifications
expected_behavior: Cuts false positive episode count by >60% on negative controls.

name: D1 Binary Median Filter (Width = 5 Windows / 150 Seconds)
group: Group L: Temporal Smoothing, Markov Decoding, and HSMM (D0, D1, D2)
hypothesis: Wider 5-window median filter provides aggressive noise suppression in noisy ambulatory wearable environments.
components_changed: Running binary median filter over window width W=5.
inputs: Window binary classifications
expected_behavior: Higher specificity, but slight boundary erosion on short paroxysmal runs.

name: D1 Binary Median + Bounded Gap Merging (< 60s Intervening Gaps)
group: Group L: Temporal Smoothing, Markov Decoding, and HSMM (D0, D1, D2)
hypothesis: Merging brief non-AF gaps (< 60s) between consecutive AF episodes repairs fragmented episodes caused by transient noise dropouts.
components_changed: D1 baseline pipeline: 3-window median filter followed by merging bounded non-AF intervals < 60s.
inputs: Timeline binary intervals
expected_behavior: Prevents episode over-counting; matches expert clinical electrophysiologist annotation.

name: D1 Binary Median + Bounded Gap Merging (< 120s Intervening Gaps)
